prompt.context: Your client is a national manufacturer of white goods (fridges, stoves, etc.). They have approached us because their market share has been declining over the past few years and they want to know what they should do.
prompt.question: What should the client do to reverse its declining market share?

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive landscape like?
clarifying_info.a: Competition has been flat. New entrants into the retail channel, such as Best Buy, have put pressure on the client's business.

clarifying_info.q: How is the client's product priced relative to the market?
clarifying_info.a: The product is currently premium priced at 25% above market price. There are two other price tiers: mid and low.

clarifying_info.q: What are the typical margin structures for retailers and manufacturers?
clarifying_info.a: Retailers make on average 10% margin; manufacturers make 20% margin.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's operational situation?
clarifying_info.a: The client has several manufacturing facilities running at roughly 85–90% capacity. The business is relatively optimized right now.

framework: Understand the root cause of market share decline — channel pressure from new retail entrants (e.g., Best Buy) vs. pricing vs. product
Assess the client's pricing position — premium tier at 25% above market; evaluate whether pricing is sustainable or needs adjustment
Evaluate channel strategy — current reliance on retailers vs. potential to open own retail shops
Explore incentive structures with key retail partners to motivate them to push the client's premium products
Identify new customer segments — e.g., commercial/contractor business to broaden the customer base
Consider operational leverage — capacity at 85–90%, so volume growth is feasible without major capex

questions.prompt: What are the three key strategic areas the client should investigate to counter the pressure from Best Buy?
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies three levers: (1) opening own retail shops to bypass retailer margin pressure and control the brand experience; (2) building an incentive plan for Best Buy to motivate them to push the client's premium-priced products; (3) expanding into commercial/contractor channels to build a new customer base independent of consumer retail.

questions.prompt: Given that retailers earn 10% and manufacturers earn 20%, and the product is priced 25% above market, how does Best Buy's entry affect the client's economics?
questions.guidance: Best Buy, as a large-format retailer with strong buyer power, can demand better terms, compressing the manufacturer's 20% margin or forcing price concessions. The 25% premium positioning is at risk if Best Buy promotes lower-priced competitors more aggressively. Candidate should note the leverage dynamic: the client needs Best Buy more than Best Buy needs any single supplier.

brainstorming.prompt: What options does the client have to grow or protect its market share given the channel and pricing pressures?

categories.name: Channel Strategy
ideas: Open proprietary retail stores to control brand experience and avoid retailer margin squeeze
Partner with specialty kitchen/appliance boutiques to reinforce premium positioning

categories.name: Retailer Incentives
ideas: Create a co-op advertising program with Best Buy and other retailers
Offer volume rebates or sell-through bonuses tied to premium SKU performance
Provide in-store display allowances and trained brand ambassadors

categories.name: New Customer Segments
ideas: Target commercial/contractor channel (property developers, hotels, restaurants)
Develop a builder/developer program for new residential construction
Offer leasing or subscription models for commercial clients

categories.name: Pricing & Product
ideas: Introduce a mid-tier sub-brand to capture price-sensitive consumers without cannibalizing the premium line
Bundle products (fridge + stove) to increase average transaction value
Offer extended warranty or service contracts to justify premium pricing

categories.name: Operations & Cost
ideas: Use spare capacity (10–15% headroom) to produce more volume if new channels are developed
Evaluate supply chain efficiency to protect margins under pricing pressure

recommendation: The client should pursue three parallel strategies to reverse market share decline: (1) open its own retail shops to reduce dependence on Best Buy and reinforce premium brand positioning; (2) design a targeted incentive program for Best Buy to motivate sales staff to recommend and push the client's premium products; (3) build a commercial/contractor sales channel to diversify the customer base beyond consumer retail.
risks: Opening own retail is capital-intensive and operationally complex — requires real estate, staffing, and brand execution capabilities
Incentive programs with Best Buy may only provide short-term relief if the underlying margin math does not work for the retailer
Commercial/contractor channel has longer sales cycles and requires a different go-to-market capability
next_steps: Conduct a feasibility study for owned retail (pilot one or two flagship stores in high-density markets)
Negotiate a structured incentive and co-marketing agreement with Best Buy
Map the commercial/contractor landscape and identify the top 20 target accounts for a direct sales pilot
